alex: Heads up — saw a perf regression on Mixtral MoE after the kernel selector change midday. p95 token latency jumped ~2.3x and tail GPU utilization dropped. KV cache eviction rate spiked at the same time. anyone looking?
jen: yep i noticed traffic spike + deploy at 11:34 hitting --kernel=avx_softmax_v2. quick diff in deploy logs: `runtime.flags: kernel_selector=auto->avx_softmax_v2`
sam: ran a quick nsight trace on a repro shard. highlights: GPU SM efficiency down ~18%, memcpy time up 40ms total, router CPU time +30%. also saw more host<->device roundtrips when expert fanout > 3.
perf-bot: ALERT perf/regression: service=mixtral-moe, metric=p95_token_latency, delta=+2.3x, deploy=sha@b3f4a2, samples=1200, window=15m
maya: initial hypothesis: kernel switch improved single-expert softmax but interacts poorly with our top-k routing pattern -> more partial-expert invocations and KV cache churn (evictions and reloads). that increases memcpy and reduces effective batch packing.
alex: that matches what i saw in the memory counters — eviction count from the KV store doubled. i think two failure modes: (1) more experts per request -> fanout and smaller per-expert batches, (2) the new softmax kernel has worse throughput for tiny batches.
jen: can we try: (A) limit router.top_k to 1 or 2 on canary for this model, (B) force kernel fallback for batch_size < 8 to scalar_softmax, (C) experiment with increasing KV cache size by 20% on a canary pool?
sam: i prototyped (B) locally — added heuristic in kernel selector: `if batch_size < 8 -> use scalar_softmax` — on microbench for tiny batches p50 improved ~15%, p95 improved ~28%.
maya: for (A) i worry lowering top_k hurts quality. proposal: route 80% of canary traffic with top_k=1 and 20% with top_k=4, compare latency + topk-loss on our eval set.
alex: agree. add (C) too — make cache size param injectable per canary pool. also enable KV eviction logging at debug for 1h.
jen: sample canary config (yaml):
```
canaries:
  mixtral-moex:
    routes:
      - weight: 80
        router.top_k: 1
      - weight: 20
        router.top_k: 4
    runtime_flags:
      kernel_selector:
        small_batch_fallback: scalar_softmax
    kv_cache:
      capacity_multiplier: 1.2
      eviction_log: debug
```

sam: i'll spin the canary during low-traffic window 02:00-04:00 UTC. i'll collect nsight and our router traces.
maya: also add a short profiler hook to record per-expert batch sizes and per-request fanout in the trace so we can correlate with memcpy spikes.
alex: ok owners: sam -> canary deploy + nsight traces; jen -> implement small-batch kernel fallback flag in selector; maya -> tracing/metric additions and eval metric for top-k quality; alex -> coordinate canary and rollback guard. target: run canary tonight and reconvene after 3h of traffic.
jen: one more note — add a quick safety: if canary p95 > baseline * 1.5 -> automatic rollback. i can wire that into rollout service.

alex: thanks team. i'll post results in this thread once we have traces. :thumbsup:
